title: Prefix coalescer and discrete TTL calibrator for cost smoothing
creator: Lena Park
description: Introduce a prefix coalescing layer and a discrete TTL calibration engine that automatically proposes conservative TTL buckets per prefix-popularity quantile. This ticket covers model design, offline simulator, telemetry queries, a shadow canary rollout plan that exercises batching interactions, and a safe rollback path. Goal: reduce per-token cost by increasing effective cache hit-rate without violating latency SLOs or materially degrading downstream model quality.
acceptance_criteria: Offline simulator can ingest 28 days of prefix traces and produce estimate of expected hit-rate uplift and cost delta
Automated TTL proposals generated for top 10k prefixes with confidence intervals and monotonic TTL mapping across popularity quantiles
Shadow canary (10% traffic) runs for 72 hours with automated safety gates: no >3% tail-latency regression, hit-rate uplift within simulator CI, and <2% increase in failed responses
Playbooked rollback triggers and automated rollback runbook verified in staging
Design review and PM signoff obtained; implementation PR merged with unit + e2e tests
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Picked discrete TTL buckets (e.g., 0s, 30s, 2m, 10m, 1h) instead of per-prefix continuous TTL to simplify rollout and auditing (decision by Eng leads)
2026-03-12: Use popularity quantiles (top 0.1%, 0.1-1%, 1-5%, 5-20%, rest) for TTL mapping; monotonic mapping enforced via isotonic regression to avoid non-intuitive assignments
2026-03-13: Coalescing strategy: group prefixes using suffix-trie similarity + domain-safe override file; avoid grouping prefixes marked as high-safety or PII-sensitive
2026-03-13: Batching interaction: ensure prefix coalescer exposes hint headers to runtime so batching can preserve latency-sensitive routes
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Local: run simulator on sampled trace, generate TTL proposals and human readable diff
Stage 1 - Canary (shadow): apply TTL proposals in shadow for 10% of traffic for 72h; capture hit-rate, cost-est, p95/p99 latency, and error rates
Stage 2 - Throttle rollout: incremental apply at 10% -> 30% -> 60% over 3 days if safety gates pass
Safety gates: p99 latency increase <= 3% absolute, average cost/unit decreases >= 1% vs baseline OR hit-rate uplift >= 2%; if any gate fails, auto-roll back
Final: full apply with telemetry retention extended for 30 days and periodic re-calibration job scheduled weekly
rollback_playbook: If canary fails: immediately flip TTL assignments to previous snapshot via config version tag and halt scheduled re-calibrations
Notify on-call SRE and create incident channel; collect pcap/traces for impacted shards
If partial rollout fails: throttle back to last passing percentage and run targeted shadow tests on affected prefixes
Post-mortem: add failing prefixes to 'do-not-coalesce' list and annotate root cause
implementation_notes: Hit-rate model: use decaying-window estimator with per-prefix exponential smoothing (alpha tuned by prefix recency), combined with Bayesian shrinkage toward global mean for low-frequency prefixes
TTL calibration: map popularity quantiles to discrete TTL bins via monotonic regression; incorporate cost-utility objective: expected tokens saved * token-cost - risk_penalty
Coalescer: build prefix similarity index using n-gram suffix trie and Jaccard similarity on normalized tokenized prefixes; add whitelist/blacklist override from product rules
Shadow traffic: implement via runtime header X-KV-Coalesce:shadow-version and downstream metrics tagging to avoid user-visible behavior change
Batching: expose per-prefix 'safety_hint' (latency-sensitive | best-effort) so batching engine can prioritize small-window batching for latency-sensitive groups
Storage: store TTL proposals and versioned config in Config DB with immutability for auditing and ability to revert by tag
telemetry_queries: grafana: prefix_hit_rate: sum(kv_hits{env="prod"}) by (prefix_version) / sum(kv_lookups{env="prod"}) by (prefix_version)
cost_query: estimated_token_cost = sum(rate(tokens_generated[1m])) * unit_cost_per_token tagged by model and route

notes: Avoid over-coalescing: grouping broad prefixes can artificially inflate cache hit-rate but may hide regression risk for critical routes
For low-frequency prefixes, prefer conservative TTLs and rely on prefetching heuristics rather than long TTLs
Plan to run a weekly re-calibration job that recommends incremental changes; major changes require manual approval
